Subject: 5/5 — Excellent fit, careful drawing review, and delivery well ahead of schedule

5 stars. Arroyo Precision Works made an adapter plate and a light baffle tube for our near-IR camera, and I would happily use them again. These parts are needed for our Palomar observing run starting November 18, so both the fit and the delivery date really mattered. They delivered in 9 days against a quoted lead time of 21 days. The larger vendor we approached had quoted six weeks.

What impressed me most was that they actually read the drawing and thought about whether it made sense before cutting metal. Tiff caught a bolt-circle dimension that I had copied from an older camera drawing: I had left it as 4.125 on a sheet where the other dimensions were in millimeters, when it should have been 4.125 inches, or about 104.8 mm. That mistake was entirely mine. Ruben emailed to confirm the intended dimension, pointing out that the literal millimeter value would put the screws inside the bore. I confirmed the correction before they cut. That check saved us from getting a beautifully machined part that would have been completely unusable, and from losing time we did not have before the run. Please pass particular thanks to Tiff for catching it.

The parts passed our fit test on Monday, November 9. All eight screws on the adapter plate went into the dewar without forcing anything. We measured flatness across the face at less than 0.01 mm on our dial indicator. The baffle threads were smooth, and the black anodizing on both parts was even, with no bare spots. We also checked for light leaks with the lab lights on using a 300-second dark frame; the result was the same as with the dewar closed. For our application, those are much more useful checks than simply saying the parts looked nice, although they did look nice too.

Ruben brought the finished parts to Robinson himself, at no additional delivery charge. After worrying about whether we would have everything ready in time, I was honestly so relieved I nearly hugged him. Getting the parts early also gave us time to do the fit and dark tests before heading to the telescope, rather than discovering a problem at the last minute.

For other labs comparing suppliers: this was a two-part prototype order in black-anodized 6061-T6 aluminum, and our price included a rush setup fee. I would not assume every order will have the same turnaround. But on this job, Arroyo beat their own promised schedule by a substantial margin, caught a consequential drawing error, and delivered parts that worked on the first fit.

I would strongly support adding Arroyo to our preferred vendor list. Based on this experience, they are a shop I would trust with another time-sensitive instrument job—not just because they were fast, but because they were careful while being fast.
